security_spec.violation_condition: Linux kernel on RISC-V writes xiselect to a value in the range 0x1000–0x1100 and then accesses xireg4–xireg6, or on XLEN=64 writes an odd xiselect in that range and then accesses any xireg, triggering an illegal instruction exception that the kernel does not expect or handle gracefully at that point
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csr_write(CSR_XISELECT, ...) followed by csr_read/ csr_write(CSR_XIREG[4-6], ...) with iselect value in [0x1000, 0x1100); or on XLEN=64, any loop iterating xiselect over the iprio indirect-access range with stride 1 instead of stride 2
security_spec.summary: Previously readable/reserved indirect CSR slots (xireg4–xireg6, and odd xiselect indices on RV64) in the APLIC iprio range now mandate illegal-instruction traps, so any kernel code that probes or iterates these indices expecting silent zero/ignore behavior will take an unhandled trap and panic
